dedupe_keys.name: household level disaggregated hourly synthetic residential energy use profiles for the united states

description: This dataset gives hourly energy use profiles for millions of synthetic households across the contiguous United States for 2014, disaggregated into thermostatically controlled loads and appliance use, released by Swapna Thorve and colleagues on the University of Virginia Dataverse. The framework is bottom-up: end uses are modelled from diverse open-source surveys and first-principles models, and the authors validated results extensively against reported energy use data. They present it as a digital twin of residential energy use for studying demand response and the effects of weather, prices, electric vehicles, solar and occupancy schedules at household resolution. The data were published on the University of Virginia Dataverse on 14 December 2022, with a total size the record gives as about 30 TB, and described in Scientific Data in February 2023. Coverage: the contiguous United States, one year (2014). Access: free from the Dataverse. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Caveats: households are synthetic, so individual profiles are modelled, not metered, and the volume makes selective download necessary; the Dataverse API listed no files at the top level when read. Simulation uses: residential demand inputs for agent-based energy, grid and demand response studies at county to national scale. Related records: ResStock and the BuildingsBench Buildings-900K dataset.
